newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem in Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem in Pakistani city.

text.p: Two men on a motorcycle shot dead an elderly Shi'ite Moslem shopkeeper in the Pakistani city of Lahore on Monday in what police said appeared to be a sectarian killing.
They said the gunmen fired on Hakim Salamat Jafri, 75, as he sat in his shop selling traditional medicines, killing him instantly.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, which was assumed to be the latest incident in a long-running feud between militant Sunni and Shi'ite groups in Pakistan.
In another incident, two men accosted a Sunni Moslem activist, Majid Raza, and bundled him into a vehicle in the Punjab provincial town of Jhang on Monday.
Police said Raza, a retired army captain, had just returned to Jhang, his home town, after spending two years in jail in connection with the murder of a Shi'ite leader.
Punjab police detained 13 activists from rival Sunni and Shi'ite groups on Monday under a plan to seize 100 militants ahead of the Shi'ite mourning festival of Ashura next month.
Police were also seeking 46 proclaimed offenders accused of involvement in sectarian violence over the past six months.
Sunni-Shi'ite unrest often coincides with Ashura, which commemorates the death of Hussain, son of the Prophet Mohammad's cousin and son-in-law Ali, at the battle of Karbala in AD 680.
